title: Strings with NEL, LS, PS and a byte order mark
notes: YAML 1.2 reads these four characters as ordinary text, but YAML 1.1 reads NEL, LS and PS as line breaks, and a byte order mark is a stream marker rather than text. The family writes them as escapes in a double-quoted scalar, so every reader keeps them. A byte order mark written raw outside a quoted scalar is not valid YAML at all (it is not a character of plain or block scalars), so that fails the loose verdict too. The Core-schema reading (loose) is the specification. The reading under YAML 1.1 and the number forms that some common readers accept (strict) is a writing convention of the family: a string is written plain only when it reads as that same string there too.
